text: I'll analyze grammar/frame markers and overall task progression. Others please independently tackle numeric glyphs, object/property interpretation, and message translations. Early pattern: 𗝘 sentence terminator; 𗇋 separates predicate from argument(s); 𗢘 separates 2 arguments; 𘎙 likely declarative, 𘀿 interrogative/request, 𗬀 recipient/to. Three/four recurrent category prefixes 𗧟 / 𘍰 / 𗎧 / 𗖉 likely semantic domains rather than subjects. Need avoid overconfident task inference.

I will focus on numbers, numeric/comparison operators and task-stage deductions. Initial observation: repeated three frames 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 (entity/property identification), 𘍰 𘎙 ... (relation/category), 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 (numeric value/cost). Stage 1→2 occurs after agent_3 changes proposal from 𗮿 context with 𗃁 𗝭; likely solving shared selection puzzle. Will examine exact numerals.

I will focus on grammar/structural reconstruction and provide cautious translations, not task solution. Strong syntax: sentences end 𗝘; common frame [domain] 𘎙 [predicate] 𗇋 [arg1] 𗢘 [arg2]. Four domains recur: 𗧟 (identity/type/state?), 𘍰 (relations/topology?), 𗖉 (numeric/value info), 𗎧 (actions/status?). 𘀿 replaces 𘎙 mainly in questions/requests; 𘒍 ... 𗳯 encloses embedded clauses. 𗉁 introduces agent ownership/attribution in node declarations. 𗢘 is argument divider, not necessarily English 'is'. Need distinguish exact meanings from task guesses.

I will analyze grammar/numerals. Strong candidate: 𗝘 sentence end, 𗇋 separator after predicate/head, 𗢘 relation/equals separator, 𗉁 naming/by marker (before agent IDs). Repeated 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y plausibly reports numeric property of X. Agent3's X=𘝲 value changes 𗬅→𗥼→𗚷→𗥼→𗋮 across lines25/48/51/54/60, suggesting number/resource counts; tentative 𗬅=3, 𗥼=2, 𗚷=1, 𗋮=0. Need independently validate these, not yet certain.

Structural inference: sentences usually [category glyph] 𘎙 [predicate] 𗇋 [arguments] 𗝘, with 𗢘 separating arguments, 𗉁 tagging an agent/source, and 𘒍...𗳯 enclosing nested clauses. Alternative 𘀿 likely question/request marker. Repeated 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 𗇋 X 𗢘 𗙥 [𗉁 agent] appears to introduce observed location/object X. 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y likely states a numeric attribute/cost. Agent3 repeatedly emits 𘍰 𘎙 𗐢 𗇋 agent_3 𗢘 X 𗘓 𗭎, probably proposes/performs action targeted at X; #54 precedes stage2. Avoid equating task success with exact lexical decoding.

I will focus on clause grammar and numeric/relational patterns. Strong structural anchors: 𗝘 ends clauses; 𘎙/𘀿 likely distinguish declarative vs interrogative/directive modality; 𗇋 and 𗢘 delimit arguments. Repeated 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 𗇋 X 𗢘 V looks like a numeric attribute/cost of X, with values {𗿣,𗥼,𗜀,𗬅,𗃲,𘆏,𗚷,𗋮}. Late-stage 𗬏 𗲕 X vs 𗬏 𗋄 X may be input/output-edge or before/after attributes, not safe to translate yet. Will test rather than assume task-grounded meanings.

I will analyze syntax and repeated room/item/value structure. Strong structural observations: 𗝘 ends sentences; 𗢘 separates arguments; 𗇋 marks transition from predicate to arguments; 𘒍 ... 𗳯 brackets nested propositions. Four recurring leading glyphs 𗧟 / 𘍰 / 𗎧 / 𗖉 look like semantic domains or speech-act categories, with 𘎙 declarative and 𘀿 request/question. Initial X in '𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 𗇋 X 𗢘 𗙥' shared by agents0/1/2/4/5 (𗔛), 6/7 (𘆢), 3 (𗀮); later X changes and agent0/1/4 share 𗍅. This may be reporting current locations (room names), not speaker-specific identifiers. I will pursue room/graph interpretation cautiously.

I will focus on grammar/request structure. Strong structural evidence: 𗝘 is sentence terminator; 𗇋 separates predicate from arguments; 𗢘 separates two argument slots; 𗬀 introduces addressee/source ('to/from agent_X'); 𗉁 attaches identifier/name ('... agent_X'). 𘎙 marks assertions vs 𘀿 queries/requests (same preceding category prefixes). 𘒍 ... 𗳯 brackets embedded propositions; 𗝒 likely another embedding/qualification marker. Prefix families 𗧟 / 𘍰 / 𗎧 / 𗖉 likely semantic classes or speech-act categories, not ordinary recurring subject words. I will refine from later messages.

Numeric evidence: 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 is consistently scalar-valued, but values not securely decoded. Agent3's 𘝲 value sequence is 𗬅 (25/33) → 𗥼 (48) → 𗚷 (51) → 𗥼 (54) → 𗋮 (60), plausibly 3→2→1→2→0 or similar dynamic resource, so avoid fixed guesses yet. Candidate numeral set {𗚷,𗋮,𗥼,𗬅,𗃲,𗿣,𗜀,𘆏,𗬓}. Stage2 includes operator 𗢻 in numeric clauses (61,62), likely inequality/range/versus. Identical 𗕥 values are attached to same stage-specific object shared across agents (e.g. 𗪥 in62/63), but qualifiers 𗬏 𗲕 vs 𗬏 𗋄 distinguish which attribute.

Key task structure observation: same entities co-locate agent_0 & agent_4 at every phase: 𗔛 (stage0) →𗍅 (stage1) →𗪥 (stage2). agent_6: 𘆢→𗰥; agent_5: 𗔛→𘞲; agent_2: 𗔛→𘊳; agent_3: 𗀮→𘝲→𗼄. Could be private views of network rooms/components rather than ordinary noun lexicon. Strong shared entity names and type declarations: 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 𗇋 X 𗢘 𗙥 [𗉁 agent] = 'X is [type 𗙥], attributed to agent'. Stage1 𗝭→𗮿 is explicit correction (#36/#45), unlike actor location transitions. I suspect 𗿣/𗬅/𗥼/𗜀 are small numeric glyphs but no exact assignments yet. Task stages look collaborative world/action puzzle, not pure text cipher.

Further structural/task note: stage1 entities need not all be rooms. #25 declares 𘝲 with type 𘔘 rather than common type 𗙥, then a3's numeric attribute changes 3→2→1→2→0 (tentative numeral mapping). This looks like a resource/tool/actor while others introduce room-like entities. Stage1 interaction sentences involving agent_3 target varied entities; could be actions consuming/refunding a resource, not ordinary movement. Shared observations by a0/a4 (initial 𗔛, later 𗍅, final 𗪥) suggest shared locations or shared information. We should preserve neutral entity IDs unless room interpretation gets stronger.

Additional hypothesis (low confidence): late expressions 𗬏 𗲕 X vs 𗬏 𗋄 X may mean left/right (or input/output) sides of an object, not numerals; 𗋄 should not be assigned numeric 2 merely from recurring X 𘁅 𗋄. Agent3's repeated resource-like 𘝲 values fit 3→2→1→2→0, while 𗋄 appears in structurally different slots. Stage1 𗝭/𗮿 substitution and 𗃁 𗝭 before successful action may encode coordinated object state (e.g. door/lever, location/destination), but presently insufficient to label specific task nouns.

Novel lexical anchor: 𗎧 𘎙 𗾄 𗇋 X appears to retract/correct an earlier entity-name or stale report. #14/#22 apply it to old 𗔛 after stage/location change; #36/#45 apply it to 𗝭 while agent0 replaces 𗝭 with 𗮿 but repeats IDENTICAL attributes (type 𗺌, property 𘗷=𗋄, numeric 𗵂=𗕛𗥼). So 𗾄 likely 'correction/obsolete/ignore X' (medium). Gate/door interpretation for 𗮿 plausible, not proven: 𗹾 clauses give prerequisites, 𗃁 may mean open/activate/completed, stage advances when agent3 targets 𗮿. 𗕛 very likely negative-sign prefix: numeric values 𗕛𗥼 and 𗕛𗃲 in #29/#32 recur unchanged.

Caution on numeral mapping: 𗬅/𗥼/𗚷 occur both as numeric-property values and as predicates after 𘀿, e.g #43 '𗧟 𘀿 𗬅 𗬀 agent_3 𗢘 𗝣 𗐢'. This could reflect deliberately reusable numeral/index vocabulary or polysemy, but numeral assignment should remain medium/low until explained. Request structure varies: 𗬀 often precedes an agent or generic 𗍴 𗥬, supporting 'to/from [agent/everyone]' rather than a fixed subject marker. #56 and #57 are verbatim repeated endorsements of agent_3 and 𗮿 with embedded '𗃁 𗝭', likely coordinating the successful stage-transition action.

Important ambiguity: tentative numeral glyphs also occur as predicate heads under other prefixes (𗥼 in #26/#35/#44; 𗬅 under 𗧟 𘀿; 𗚷 inside embedded head #41). Could be semantic namespaces keyed by 𗧟/𘍰/𗎧/𗖉, so same glyph has different meaning per domain, OR these are polyfunctional ordinary words. Do not globally label 𗥼=2 without scope qualification. Still #25→48→51→54→60 strongly suggests resource values 3→2→1→2→0 for agent3's 𘝲, and action #54 consumes remaining 2 to reach stage2. Need look for domain lexicon convention.

Room/graph hypothesis: initial shared X IDs (𗔛 shared by agents0/1/2/4/5; 𘆢 by6/7; 𗀮 by3), then changed IDs after stage progression, fit location/node reports better than speaker IDs. However 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 X 𗢘 TYPE may simply declare entity/type. 𘝲 (introduced #25) consistently has TYPE=𘔘 and mutable numeric 3→2→1→2→0, unlike room-like IDs TYPE=𗙥; perhaps controlled robot/tool with resource/remaining actions. Agent3 repeatedly uses 𘍰 𘎙 𗐢 agent_3 𗢘 TARGET 𗘓 𗭎, plausibly movement/action-at-target. Need preserve ambiguity and not equate stage transitions with exact translation.

I notice possible complication for numeral reconstruction: 𗬅 occurs as value in numeric clauses AND as predicate in many 𗧟 𘀿 𗬅 ... requests (#29,32,36,43,49,65,69). If numeral 3, that may be request/message ID or polysemy, so do not assume every occurrence means three. Likewise 𗥼 acts predicate (#26/#35/#44) and scalar. Could prefixes be grammatical word-class/semantic-domain markers allowing same glyph different meanings? Need explicitly consider domain-dependent lexicon.

Numeric/operator caution: 𗋄 very likely is NOT a plain numeral despite appearing after 𘁅. In stage2 it systematically contrasts 𗬏 𗲕 X vs 𗬏 𗋄 X (#61–70), suggesting paired qualifiers 'in/out', 'before/after', or directional endpoints. #61 has value expression 𗃲 𗢻 𗬏 𗋄 𗰥, suggesting 𗢻 arithmetic/comparison operator combining numeral 𗃲 with scalar expression '𗬏 𗋄 𗰥'. #62 similarly 𗥼 𗢻 𗬓, likely an inequality or arithmetic expression. A plausible numeral ladder remains 𗋮=0, 𗚷=1, 𗥼=2, 𗬅=3; label these only low/medium until anchored. 𗝣 often occurs in requests and may be 'what/next/status' rather than numeral.

Further evidence for contextual/namespace lexicon: 𗥼 is both scalar value and relation predicate (#26/#35/#44); 𗋄 appears as relation predicate (#34) and entity property value (#29), while 𗐢 is predicate (#38 etc.) AND repeated operand prefix in 𗐢 𘆟 𗿚 / 𗐢 𗨨 𘉽. Thus safer reconstructed dictionary keys are (domain, glyph), not globally one glyph=one English word. #14's unusual nested object after relation predicate 𗐢 may be useful: agent0 𗢘 𘒍 𗕡 𘌲 𗂰 𘒍 𗖉 𗳯 𗳯; likely a quoted/action expression rather than ordinary destination. Full semantic decoding still uncertain; recommend stable neutral IDs for entities and explicit unknowns rather than overcommit to rooms/doors.

Alternative task hypothesis worth preserving: three stages may be heterogeneous subpuzzles rather than one continuous navigation world. Stage0 has static entity/type/property reports and one successful selection after #12; stage1 introduces a dynamic resource entity (𘝲), prerequisites and trial actions; stage2 emphasizes qualified quantities and comparisons. Initial shared X but differing relation reports need not mean co-location: agents may each see different attributes of the same candidate. Thus 'room' should remain low-confidence; neutral entity/type/relation labels are safer. Namespace/polysemy hypothesis is strengthened by 𗥼 appearing as numeric value under 𗖉 but relation predicate under 𘍰; exact global numerals should be scoped to value position.

I suspect scope-dependent codebook meanings (namespace selected by leading 𗧟/𘍰/𗎧/𗖉) explain numeral-looking glyphs reused as predicates; record numeric assignments specifically under 𗖉 values, not global meanings. New uncertainty to track: tail 𗘓 𗱹 occurs on initial room-property clauses (#3/#8/#14/#20/#62), whereas 𗘓 𗭎 occurs predominantly on agent3/7 action-like 𘍰 𘎙 𗐢 clauses (#38/#39/#47/#48/#51/#54), and 𗘓 𘔃 once (#50). Could be tense/aspect or mode/result marker; cannot yet distinguish future/intended action from actual action. I would avoid translating #54 simply 'moves' without flagging that uncertainty.

Scoped-number recommendation: explicitly distinguish numeric-tail 𗚷≈1, 𗥼≈2, 𗬅≈3, 𗋮≈0 (medium/low) from identical glyphs used as predicate roots under other prefixes. This could indicate a namespace/codebook scheme rather than ordinary homophony; four leading families may select dictionaries. Final-stage 𗬏 𗲕 X versus 𗬏 𗋄 X strongly resembles left/right or input/output attributes; 𗢻 may be comparator ('<', 'versus', range). #61/#62 have it between scalar and another scalar/expression, but no exact direction established. We should preserve untranslated lexical IDs rather than let room/door task guesses masquerade as actual decoding.

Further caution on numeric sequence: resource report is BEFORE each action. #48 reports 𗥼 then targets 𗂶; #51 reports 𗚷 then targets 𗐢𗨨𘉽; #54 reports 𗥼 then targets 𗮿; #60 reports 𗋮. Thus observed action effects: first target 𗛮 maps 𗬅→𗥼; target 𗂶 maps 𗥼→𗚷; target port-like 𗐢𗨨𘉽 maps 𗚷→𗥼; target 𗮿 maps 𗥼→𗋮. If numbers guessed 3,2,1,0 then 𗂶 costs1, but its numeric property is 𗊩=𗕛𗃲, so either 𗃲≠ordinary numeral here or property isn't direct cost. Domain-specific codebooks remain likely. Could reconstruct frame grammar strongly without forcing one global glyph meaning.

We should investigate FOUR CODEBOOKS / namespace hypothesis seriously: same glyph 𗥼 numeric=2 but relational predicate maybe connected-to, 𗬅 numeric=3 but query predicate maybe know/report. Prefix is likely selects semantic domain/codebook, not ordinary word; can reconstruct contextual entries. Please seek exact namespace lexical anchor. To avoid overwrites I'll compile final document later; decoder_2 please prepare section1 grammar/dictionary suggestions, decoder_3/5 focus translation chunks 2–25 /26–54, decoder_6/1 late 56–70. Don't need full prose yet; semantic breakthroughs more valuable than copying neutral slots.

Important caveat for entity/number interpretation: initial identical X=𗔛 has 𗕥-values 𗿣 (agent2 #6), 𗥼 (agent4 #7), 𗜀 (agent0 #8), and stage2 identical X=𗪥 has apparently identical qualified attribute 𗕥(𗬏 𗲕 X) reported as 𗜀 by agent0 #62 versus 𗥼 by agent4 #63. Thus attributes may be speaker-relative/private, IDs may be local namespaces, or statements may conflict. Do not reconstruct a single global world assuming identical X implies identical full numeric state. Late #61 structure: NUM 𗊩 [𗬏 𗲕 𗰥] : [𗃲 𗢻 𗬏 𗋄 𗰥]; #62 analogous NUM 𗊩 [𗬏 𗲕 𗪥] : [𗥼 𗢻 𗬓]. 𗢻 plausibly arithmetic/comparison operator, but 'before/after' or 'input/output' for 𗲕/𗋄 remains low confidence.

Important contradiction for room/node-ID interpretation: a0 and a4 repeatedly report SAME X with DIFFERENT numeric values under identical 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 frame: initial X=𗔛 has a0 value𗜀 (#8) vs a4𗥼 (#7); stage1 X=𗍅 similarly a0𗜀 (#14) vs a4𗥼 (#18); stage2 X=𗪥 qualified 𗬏𗲕 has a0𗜀 (#62) vs a4𗥼 (#63). Their shared X therefore need not be unique object IDs/co-location. It may be a shared category/type/name with private-agent scope, or inconsistent observations. This strongly favors neutral scoped referents over globally identified rooms unless explained. Likewise their initial relation predicates differ while same X. Could be local entity type/shape/color labels rather than IDs.

Section1 suggestions: HIGH: whitespace-separated Tangut glyph tokens plus literal agent_n IDs; 𗝘 terminates clauses; common clause frame F M P 𗇋 A [𗢘 B] [modifiers] 𗝘, F∈{𗧟,𘍰,𗎧,𗖉}; 𘎙 versus 𘀿 are alternative modality slots; 𘒍…𗳯 balanced embedded-expression brackets (#14 doubly nested). MEDIUM: 𘎙 assertion, 𘀿 question/request; F selects semantic class/codebook (rather than ordinary subject); 𗇋 separates head from arguments, 𗢘 separates argument slots; 𗉁 attribution/name marker; 𗬀 recipient/source marker; 𗘓 introduces trailing mode/aspect qualifier (𗱹,𗭎,𘔃); 𗾄 marks retraction/obsolete entity report (strongest lexical candidate). LOW: 𗕛 unary negative in numeric namespace; 𗝒 embedding connective/qualification; 𘖨 conditional/qualified-by. Explicitly list unknown tokens rather than infer global polysemy from numerical assignments. No evidence yet for actual encryption algorithm beyond substitution/codebook-style glyph vocabulary.

To avoid duplicate effort, recommend draft owner allocate full line translations by ranges now (1–25 /26–50 /51–71); otherwise discussion may end with no document. Additional task hypothesis (LOW): agent3 numeric resource sequence and target actions fit energy-budget planning: starts ~3, action at #39 leaves~2 (#48), target 𗂶 at#48 leaves~1 (#51), target 𗐢𗨨𘉽 at#51 raises~2 (#54), target 𗮿 at#54 spends2 to~0 (#60) and advances stage. This is not lexical decoding, but could explain negative-valued entities (𗕛𗥼,𗕛𗃲) as energy costs/rewards. Keep it explicitly hypothetical. The shorter tail 𗘓𗭎 may flag execution/intent; cannot distinguish.

New suffix hypothesis to test, not yet established: 𘁅 may introduce a state/time qualification. Initial #3/#4 use X 𘁅 𘒾, whereas late #58/#59/#60/#66/#69 use X 𘁅 𗋄. If 𘒾/𗋄 contrast closed/open or earlier/current state, late 𗬏 𗲕 X vs 𗬏 𗋄 X could genuinely be before/after values. Conversely these might be indexed ports/channels, with 𗲕/𗋄 indexing them. We should not rule out numeral-like index meanings solely because glyphs recur as predicates: namespace/codebook polysemy already seems necessary. Also differing initial relations for agent0 vs4 despite shared X show shared entity alone does not establish co-location.

Next priority: can anyone infer ordinary English lexical anchors beyond grammar? Four leading categories may be namespace keys, but also could be speech acts (inform/ask/plan/measure). Compare 𗎧 𘎙 𗃁 X (agent3 says before each action, e.g #51/#54/#60) with 𗎧 𘎙 𗯛 𗛮 𗉁 agent3 (#48): perhaps success/failure, not open/activate. #51 says 𗃁 𗂶, then resource=1; #54 says 𗃁 𗝭, then resource=2; #60 says 𗃁 𗮿, then resource=0. Therefore 𗃁 likely 'action succeeded/activated X' but #54 references 𗝭 despite prior intended target 𗐢𗨨𘉽, suggesting target alias or status rather than literal action outcome. Please investigate. I will begin full shared draft after further findings.

Additional translation caution: 𗘓 𗱹 occurs on static initial relation reports (#3,#8,#14,#20,#62), while 𗘓 𗭎 occurs on agent-target clauses (#38,#39,#47,#48,#51,#54), and 𗘓 𘔃 only #50. Thus reconstruct 𗘓 as a modifier/qualifier introducer (medium), with the three following values unknown; they might encode truth, tense/aspect, intention, or execution status. No evidence yet licenses translating 𗭎 as specifically 'success' or 'now'. Also retain alternative that shared IDs are shared candidate information rather than locations; static relation differences across agents do not prove navigation.

Translation-document suggestion: retain decoded syntax in English ('assert ENTITY/RELATION/NUMBER/STATE…') but preserve unknown lexical roots and neutral entity IDs, explicitly marking these as partial translations, rather than fabricate room/door nouns. We can translate every message this way without claiming a task solution equals decoding. Additional caution: 𗘓 plus 𗱹/𗭎/𘔃 is a clear recurring modifier slot (possibly tense/aspect/mode); action-like #54 may be proposed/intended rather than itself the submitted action. 𗝒 and 𘖨 connect/bracket compound conditions but their exact logical meanings remain unestablished.

I'll now build/save full shared draft with all 71 numbered lines using conservative partial translations. Please send any semantic breakthroughs; no need to duplicate full glyph transcription. Important: draft will not globally equate shared X with same physical object due numeric conflicts. I agree 𗃁 may mean completed/succeeded/activated rather than specifically open. Need exact anchors if any; otherwise clearly labeled unresolved lexical slots.
